vibe.rationale: Vibe 4 — upgraded from 3 (lower edge) on the strength of the June 12 Pakistani PM 'final, agreed-upon text' announcement and Trump's 'maybe over the weekend in Europe' signing window signal. Four factors define the June 13 evening upgrade and three factors sustain the ceiling at 4. Upgrade factors: (1) Pakistani PM 'final text' announcement — the first externally confirmed statement that negotiators have concluded a final text; this is qualitatively more specific than the prior 'closing in' / 'gaps reduced' / 'broad principles' language that characterized the late-May and early-June cycle; Pakistani PM carries unique credibility as the primary non-Gulf third-party channel (Islamabad Talks convener); (2) Trump 'weekend in Europe' signing window — the first specific geographic and temporal commitment from the president; previously Trump had described progress without a signing timeline; a specific window identification is the single most proximate deal-confirmation signal of the conflict arc; (3) Incirlik June 11 escalation resolved as March misattribution — the primary downward pressure from the June 11 brief is removed; no new NATO-territory Iranian escalation in the June 12-13 cycle; (4) Iran comms resolved Day 10 — channel integrity confirmed for 10 consecutive cycle days, longest sustained confirmed-open period of the conflict. Ceiling-at-4 factors: (1) deal unsigned, Trump approval gating — 'near-term uncertainty introduced by the presidential editing process' per CBS source; the 'final text' announcement by a third-party intermediary is distinct from a Trump signature; the Hormuz closure (Day 106) and naval blockade remain fully operative; no CENTCOM stand-down issued; Iranian drones intercepted June 12 — kinetic activity concurrent with finalization, not resolved; (2) FOMC T-3 with maximum policy complexity — Warsh inaugural meeting June 16-17; policy statement bias shift from easing to neutral is the first concrete Warsh signal; 4 FOMC dissents in April (most divided since 1992) creates elevated statement-language risk; ECB rate hike signal adds external monetary policy pressure into an already complex inflation environment (CPI 4.2%, nominal spending 5.9% QoQ annualized); (3) PNW heat wave landing on FIFA opener — Extreme Heat Warning June 14-16, 92-100°F, coincides with June 15 Belgium vs Egypt noon PT kickoff; heat stress on NIFC-FIFA co-response window at the precise moment of first Seattle match is the highest near-term operational dual-mandate test of the cycle. Upgrade to 5 requires: confirmed US-Iran signing in Europe; Hormuz reopening timeline activated; CENTCOM stand-down order issued. Drop to 3 requires: Trump 'final text' rejection or major renegotiation demand issued; new confirmed escalation event; FOMC statement triggering bond market dislocation; or major PNW ignition concurrent with heat wave.

items.summary: The June 13 evening economic brief is defined by the three-day countdown to Warsh's inaugural FOMC meeting (June 16-17) — the most anticipated single Federal Reserve event of the year. Markets are pricing a 98.3% probability of no rate move; the hold is the near-certain outcome. The policy signal is in the statement language: the June meeting is expected to mark an explicit shift from a bias toward easing to a neutral stance on rates, reflecting accumulated inflation data (May CPI 4.2% YoY — highest since April 2023; core 2.9%; nominal spending 5.9% QoQ annualized, roughly 1.9 points above the ~4% pace consistent with 2% inflation). This is Warsh's first policy statement and press conference as chair — 30 days of silence since confirmation ends with the June 17 post-meeting presser, which is the primary market-signal event of the cycle; the language of neutrality or tightening bias will define market expectations for the late-2026 rate path (~70% hike odds per CME late-2026). The April FOMC meeting produced 4 dissents — the most divided committee since 1992 — creating elevated statement-drafting complexity for Warsh's inaugural meeting; managing internal dissent while projecting a coherent new chair voice is the primary governance challenge. An additional external pressure has emerged: the ECB is signaling a rate hike that, if executed, could force a reassessment of the Fed's relative monetary policy stance at precisely the moment Warsh is attempting to define his tenure's parameters. The Brent crude picture is the primary Warsh complexity variable: the Pakistani PM 'final text' signal and Trump weekend-signing window have pushed Brent into the $90-95 easing range (Hormuz-reopening-within-30-days clause is a structural Brent ceiling signal if confirmed); a confirmed deal could relieve the energy CPI channel significantly ahead of the July FOMC meeting, but the deal remains unsigned and kinetic activity (June 12 drone intercepts) is ongoing. Warsh's inaugural meeting may be concluded before the deal signature — meaning the June 17 statement could be drafted without knowing whether the ~40% Brent YoY contribution to CPI will persist or collapse in the following 30 days.

items.summary: Four secondary infrastructure threads entering June 13 evening. First: DOE's Office of Electricity announced a $1.9B funding opportunity to accelerate grid upgrades; selections anticipated in August 2026. The announcement reflects the structural urgency of US grid modernization — grid electricity sales rising at the fastest pace since World War II, driven primarily by AI data center load (224 GW incremental through 2035). Interconnection queues at historic levels, with gigawatts of ready-to-build projects waiting years for connection studies; transmission infrastructure requires a decade or more of planning, permitting, and construction. The FY27 appropriations signal is shifting focus toward critical minerals and grid resilience over renewable energy buildout, reflecting the administration's energy-emergency positioning (DOE national energy emergency operative since 2025). Battery storage deployment in 2026 is tracking above 2025's 10+ GW full-year record, but transmission bottlenecks continue limiting integration velocity. Second: NSF Newport OR ocean observatory (last remaining PNW floating station) continues advancing toward end-of-June removal — approximately two weeks remaining. Loss of this station will degrade atmospheric river early detection, marine heat wave and fisheries forecasting, wave height and storm surge coastal emergency management, and Pacific maritime monitoring capacity. Third: Sound Transit's $34.5B funding gap remains unresolved with T-2 to FIFA Seattle's first Lumen Field match (June 15); Link Light Rail is the primary stadium transit mode; no board capital resolution or federal match alternative confirmed ahead of the opening weekend. Fourth: FEMA hurricane season remains operational on Day 13 with degraded staffing; no named storms in the June 13 evening cycle; Gulf Coast and Atlantic basin early-season monitoring continues.

items.headline: NIFC Above-Normal Day 13 — East Cascades Above Normal; Oregon 83% Drought (12 Counties); Washington Drought Day 9 (4th Year); Super El Nino 1-in-4; NSF Newport Observatory ~2 Weeks; Oregon Gray Whale 21 YTD; Portland Entering Heat Warning Sunday
items.summary: Four secondary PNW environmental and civic threads entering June 13 evening. First: PNW fire-drought conditions continue tracking above-normal with no Day 3 ignition event in the evening cycle, but the June 14-16 heat event is the most significant ignition-risk weather system to enter the region since the NIFC above-normal period began. East Cascades are explicitly above normal in the June NIFC outlook; the east-slope fire onset target of July is T-17 days and heat-accelerated drying will advance that timeline. Oregon 83% drought coverage (12 counties emergency); Washington drought emergency Day 9 (4th consecutive year). BPA hydropower output reduced; soil moisture deficits advancing; snowpack essentially gone at mid-elevations. Super El Nino (1-in-4 probability) amplifies temperature anomalies and extends the season endpoint into October. Portland has been in the high-60s to low-70s reprieve through the week, but that ends Sunday — the heat warning activates June 14 and west-slope fuel moisture advantage will dissipate rapidly over the June 14-16 window. Second: NSF Newport OR ocean observatory removal advancing at approximately two weeks from end-of-June target. Loss of this station removes the PNW's last offshore floating atmospheric river early detection and marine heat wave forecasting capacity at peak summer maritime stress. The June 14-16 heat event — arriving before the observatory's removal — illustrates precisely the forecasting capability that will be lost when the station goes dark. Third: Oregon gray whale washups continue at 21 YTD (Oregon coast), 17 YTD (Washington) — above expected annual pace, serious emaciation consistent with Pacific prey availability collapse; ocean monitoring network dismantlement concurrent with marine ecosystem stress is the PNW's long-running science infrastructure crisis. Fourth: Portland-area cooling centers, city emergency protocols, and vulnerable population services are activating ahead of the Sunday heat onset; the city's experience from the 2021 heat dome (1,000+ Oregon deaths) informs the response framework; no heat-related mortality reported in the evening cycle.

analyst_summary: June 13, 2026 evening closes at Vibe 4 — upgraded from Vibe 3 lower edge on the strength of the June 12 Pakistani PM 'final, agreed-upon text' announcement and Trump's 'maybe over the weekend in Europe' signing window. These represent the most specific deal-proximity signals of the 106-day conflict arc and the first external confirmation of a finalized negotiating text, qualifying as the genuine upgrade catalyst the June 11 brief required. The Incirlik June 11 escalation report is downgraded: investigation confirms those were March 2026 events (NATO intercepts on March 4, 9, and 13); no new June 12-13 Incirlik escalation confirmed, removing the primary downward pressure from the June 11 positioning. The deal ceiling at 4 reflects three structural incomplete states: (1) deal unsigned — Trump approval is the gating constraint, kinetic activity (June 12 dual drone intercepts) is ongoing, Hormuz closed Day 106, no CENTCOM stand-down issued; (2) FOMC T-3 — Warsh's inaugural June 16-17 meeting with policy statement bias shift from easing to neutral, 4 April dissents, ECB hike pressure, and a press conference that must calibrate an undefined deal environment; (3) PNW heat-fire-FIFA triple convergence — Extreme Heat Warning June 14-16 landing directly on the FIFA Seattle opener (June 15, noon PT, Belgium vs Egypt), NIFC-FIFA co-response fully active Day 6, east Cascades ignition risk elevated by the heat system, BPA hydropower under peak demand with drought-reduced capacity. Four primary overnight and weekend watch items: (1) Trump deal signature or delay signal — the weekend Europe signing window; confirmed signing = transformative Vibe 5 catalyst and the largest single consumer, geopolitical, and market relief event of 2026; (2) overnight PNW ignitions — the June 14-16 heat event is the highest-intensity fire ignition window since the above-normal period began; any east Cascades or Gorge ignition within the co-response window directly competes with FIFA security corridor operations; (3) Warsh June 17 press conference preparation and June 16 FOMC statement — any pre-meeting communication or early statement leak carries maximum market weight; (4) Seattle June 15 match public health and security status under 92-100°F heat warning — noon PT kickoff under direct sun at peak warning temperatures.
